The analysis is clear.

**Arithmetic on received vs. invoiced:**
- Total received across both receipts (GR-A + GR-B): Pulpen 8, Map 30, Kursi 2 — the full PO quantity.
- Invoice 0688/UMA/X/2026 (paid, 2026-10-18) plus this invoice (0697): combined quantities = Pulpen 8, Map 30, Kursi 2. That equals, not exceeds, what was received.

**Same total explanation:** Both invoices bill Pulpen 4, Map 15, Kursi 1 at identical prices (4×49,600 + 15×253,300 + 1×1,712,100 = 198,400 + 3,799,500 + 1,712,100 = 5,710,000; ×1.11 = 6,338,100). The earlier invoice matches the first delivery GR-2026-0131A (2026-10-16); this invoice matches the second delivery GR-2026-0131B (2026-10-29), and this invoice's date (2026-10-29) equals that receipt date. Clause KTR-V-011#7.2 explicitly permits partial delivery with the remainder billed after receipt.

The combined quantity fits exactly within what was received, and there is a distinct goods receipt (GR-2026-0131B) for this delivery — this is a **separate_delivery**, not a resubmission.

Note: I observe line 3 uses Rp 1,712,100 for the Kursi, whereas dog clause KTR-V-011#11.1 (effective 19 Sep 2026) sets it at Rp 1,998,000 — but the invoice at the *lower* PO price is not an overcharge, and no price issue was raised.
